newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australians support apology to "stolen generation".
newsitem.headline: Australians support apology to "stolen generation".

text.p: Two thirds of Australians want their government to apologise officially to the "stolen generation", the thousands of Aboriginal children taken from their parents in a now-condemned official policy, according to newspaper poll published on Tuesday.

The Sydney Morning Herald poll found 65 percent of people supported the key recommendation of a major government report into what has been described as a genocidal policy against minority Aboriginals -- that the national, state and territory governments apologise and acknowledge official responsibility.
But the poll also found 30 percent of those surveyed disagreed with any move to apologise.
Tens of thousands of Aboriginal child were taken from their parents between the 1880s and 1960s under welfare laws which many now condemn as being based on the idea of white racial superiority.

Prime Minister John Howard made an unexpected personal apology on Monday to the "stolen generation" just hours before his government released a human rights watchdog report which said the forced assimilation amounted to genocide.
But he stopped short of offering the official apology as called for by the Human Rights Commission in its report.
Aboriginal groups are demanding an official apology for the policy and many are also pushing for compensation for those who suffered under the scheme.
The Herald poll surveyed 2,065 people around the country by telephone over the last weekend.
